issues.legal_issue: The heirs of a tenant who died before a change making the tenancy automatically continuable by heirs could not inherit the tenant’s right to recover land after the landlord stopped cultivating it personally.
material_facts: The tenant’s tenancy was terminated and the landlord obtained possession on the ground that the land was required for personal cultivation.
The tenant died before the 1956 amendment that changed the rule governing continuation of a tenancy after a tenant’s death.
The tenant’s heirs later sought restoration, alleging that the landlord had stopped cultivating the land personally within the specified period.
issues.conclusion: The heirs had no heritable right to recover possession, and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a statutory tenancy or a particular right under it is heritable depends on the provisions of the applicable statute; it cannot be decided merely by importing general notions about statutory tenancy. Under Sections 37 and 39 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, read with Section 40 as it stood before the 1956 amendment, the tenant’s restoration right was not heritable: Section 40 then required the landlord to offer continuation to an heir, but did not deem the tenancy continued, and the Act lacked the 1939 Act’s Explanation II to Section 7 expressly including heirs. The amended Section 40 and Section 4B supported continuation and inheritance after the amendment, but did not govern a tenant who had died before it. The Court relied on Vasant Hariba Londhe v. Jagannath Ramchandra Kulkarni, and distinguished Bai Jamna v. Bai Dhani and Thakorelal v. Gujarat Revenue Tribunal because the tenant deaths there preceded the amendment. Damadilal & Ors. v. Parashram & Ors. did not establish that every statutory tenancy or right is heritable; the applicable statute must be examined.

rule.if: heirs_bring_restoration_proceeding and landlord_obtained_land_for_personal_cultivation and landlord_stopped_personal_cultivation_within_relevant_period and tenant_died_before_inheritance_change and pre_change_rule_was_offer_only

predicates.heirs_bring_restoration_proceeding: The deceased tenant’s heirs brought a proceeding seeking restoration of the land.
predicates.landlord_obtained_land_for_personal_cult: The landlord obtained possession of the land on the ground that it was required for personal cultivation.
predicates.landlord_stopped_personal_cultivation_wi: The heirs alleged that the landlord stopped cultivating the land personally within the relevant period after obtaining possession.
predicates.tenant_died_before_inheritance_change: The tenant died before the legal change that made continuation of the tenancy by heirs automatic.
predicates.pre_change_rule_was_offer_only: Under the rule applicable when the tenant died, the landlord was required to offer continuation to an heir, but the tenancy was not deemed automatically continued in the heir.

issues.definition: When heirs seek restoration after a landlord stops personally cultivating land obtained for that purpose, and the tenant died under a rule requiring only an offer of continuation rather than automatic continuation, the heirs lack the restoration right.
